facts.text: Palisades’ riverfront was once a National Landmark, where visitors can explore historic reenactments and a living‑history school program.
The Palisades Interstate Park’s 1930s heyday is captured in a New Deal film, complete with historic footage and park documents.
Fort Lee Historic Park sits atop the cliffs, offering a reconstructed Revolutionary War encampment and a visitor center that tells the area’s wartime story.
The Hudson River below the Palisades has witnessed countless historic moments, from early ferry crossings to modern military defenses.
The first concerted effort to preserve the Palisades began in the 1890s, led by the American Scenic and Historic Preservation Society.
On the clifftops, historic sites range from Skunk Hollow to Millionaire’s Row, showcasing the region’s diverse heritage.
